title: Japan Travel Guide
summary: A smart Japan travel guide that covers seasonal highlights, culture, transport, and must-see modern and traditional destinations.
bestTime: March–May for cherry blossoms and September–November for autumn colors and comfortable weather.

quickFacts.Language: Japanese; English spoken in tourist districts.
quickFacts.Visa: Visa exemption for many countries; check Japanese embassy rules before travel.
quickFacts.Transport: Japan Rail Pass can be very cost-effective for multi-city travel.

attractions.name: Tokyo
attractions.summary: A high-energy metropolis of skyscrapers, temples, shopping, and cutting-edge culture.

attractions.name: Kyoto
attractions.summary: Historic shrines, traditional tea houses, and beautiful temple gardens.

attractions.name: Osaka
attractions.summary: Food capital of Japan with street food, nightlife, and friendly locals.

attractions.name: Mount Fuji
attractions.summary: Japan’s iconic peak best seen from Lake Kawaguchi or on a Fuji Five Lakes tour.

attractions.name: Hiroshima
attractions.summary: A moving reflection on peace with a modern city and historic memorials.

cultureEtiquette: Bow politely and remove shoes where indicated.
Queue respectfully and avoid loud phone calls on public transport.
Handle money and business cards with both hands as a sign of respect.
gettingAround: Use Shinkansen bullet trains for fast intercity travel.
Load an IC card like Suica for easy city transit and convenience stores.
Rent a car only for rural regions like Hokkaido or Kyushu.
sustainability: Use public transport and avoid short internal flights.
Respect local recycling and waste separation rules.
Choose small local ryokans and sustainable hospitality options.

faqs.q: Do I need a rail pass in Japan?
faqs.a: A JR Pass is useful for long-distance travel across multiple cities and should be purchased before arrival.

faqs.q: What is the best season for Japan?
faqs.a: Cherry blossom season and autumn foliage are the two most magical times to visit.

faqs.q: Can I use credit cards everywhere?
faqs.a: Credit cards are accepted in cities, but carry cash for smaller shops and temples.
